title: Discovery and interrogatories - civil procedure tools lawyers forget
p1:
Many lawyers prepare for trial by focusing on arguments. But the biggest advantage may come before the courtroom doors even open.

Some of the strongest cases are built through tools that are often overlooked: discovery and interrogatories.
p2:
A common misconception is that these tools are just paperwork or procedural formalities. In reality, they can reveal hidden facts, expose contradictions, and force the other side to commit to a position before trial.

A well-drafted interrogatory can sometimes do more damage than a dramatic courtroom question.
p3:
Discovery allows parties to obtain relevant information, documents, and evidence from the opposing side. Interrogatories are written questions that require clear answers under legal procedure.

The practical takeaway: the lawyer who asks the right questions early often controls the direction of the case later. Preparation is not only about knowing the law; it is about uncovering the facts others may be trying to hide.
conclusion: Have you seen a case where effective discovery or interrogatories changed the entire outcome? What was the most useful question asked?
